newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Police learn about lying from Israeli first lady.
newsitem.headline: Police learn about lying from Israeli first lady.

text.p: Israeli police, learning how to tell when a suspect is lying, are studying a television interview with the nation's first lady Sara Netanyahu, says an expert who lectures the police.

Gavriel Raam, a self-described expert on non-verbal signals, told Reuters on Thursday he uses the interview with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's wife because he said her facial expressions indicate "she is trying to hide something."

Shai Bazak, the prime minister's spokesman, dismissed "as nonsense" the report of the special police training, first published on Thursday in Israel's newspaper Haaretz. "I don't want to comment on that," he told Reuters.

In the interview with Israel's Channel Two television last July, Netanyahu was asked about her widely publicised dismissal of her children's nanny. The nanny told the press she was humiliated before being tossed out of the house.

"Asked if the nanny scandal bothered her, Sara said no. But at the same moment she swallowed her lower lip. When a person says a word and swallows their lip it means they have a problem with what they just said," Raam said.
